explanation: Correct! Having access to helpful dietitians is a blessing, not a barrier. The real struggles are usually money, time, and kitchen setups. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h6)

question: A patient complains that fresh vegetables are too expensive for their weekly budget. What is the best nursing advice?

options.A: Insist that only imported fresh produce will help their condition
options.B: Suggest nutritious and affordable frozen or local seasonal options
options.C: Advise the patient to borrow money to buy groceries
options.D: Tell the patient to stop eating vegetables altogether

explanation: Wonderful clinical intuition! Always help patients find budget-friendly, local alternatives so they can stay healthy without breaking the bank. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h6)

question: How should a nurse approach dietary counselling with a patient?

options.A: An ongoing, continuous process
options.B: A purely administrative paperwork duty
options.C: A one-time hospital lecture
options.D: A task completed only upon discharge

explanation: Spot on! Nutrition is a journey, not a one-time lecture. We check in, encourage, and make adjustments as the patient heals. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h7)

question: During a follow-up visit, you notice a patient missed their nutrition goals. What should you do next?

options.A: Discharge the patient from nutrition education
options.B: Reassess barriers and adjust the plan together
options.C: Double the dietary restrictions immediately
options.D: Scold the patient for lack of self-discipline

explanation: You're developing a wonderful bedside manner! Never blame or scold. Team up with the patient to figure out what went wrong and tweak the plan together. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h7)

question: What is the main goal of food hygiene and safety practices?

options.A: To ensure food is safe and wholesome for consumption
options.B: To make meals taste better and look colorful
options.C: To make cooking faster in large kitchens
options.D: To cut down the cost of buying ingredients

explanation: Food hygiene is all about stopping contamination so the food we eat stays safe and healthy from the farm or market straight to the table! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h1)

question: Which type of food hazard includes cleaning chemicals and leftover pesticide sprays?

options.A: Physical hazards
options.B: Biological hazards
options.C: Nutritional hazards
options.D: Chemical hazards

explanation: You guessed it—chemical hazards involve toxic substances like cleaning agents and farm chemicals that accidentally get into our food supply. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h1)

question: Who counts as a 'food handler' in a hospital or school setting?

options.A: Only the head chef in charge of the menu
options.B: The health inspector who visits monthly
options.C: Anyone who touches food, equipment, or utensils during prep or serving
options.D: Patients who eat the food provided

explanation: Anyone who comes into contact with food, plates, or cooking tools is considered a food handler. Safety starts with everyone! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h2)

question: Why is the role of a food handler particularly critical in a hospital environment?

options.A: Hospital patients eat more frequently than people outside
options.B: Hospital kitchens prepare larger quantities of food than standard restaurants
options.C: Hospital patients often have weakened immune systems that make them vulnerable to infections
options.D: Hospital food handlers are required to have medical degrees

explanation: Vulnerable patients in healthcare facilities suffer severe complications from foodborne illnesses that healthy people might overcome easily. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h2)

question: Which virus is famous for spreading quickly through food when infected workers don't wash their hands well?

options.A: Rabies virus
options.B: Influenza virus
options.C: Varicella virus
options.D: Norovirus

explanation: Norovirus and Hepatitis A are notorious tummy bugs spread by infected food handlers when hands aren't washed properly. Hand hygiene is key! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h3)

question: How do most harmful bacteria in food usually get passed around?

options.A: Through skin-to-skin contact between diners and waiters
options.B: By breathing in air in a crowded dining room
options.C: From mosquito bites near kitchen drains
options.D: Through the fecal-oral route via dirty hands, water, or food

explanation: It sounds unpleasant, but germs from waste easily reach food through poor handwashing—this is what we call the fecal-oral route. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h3)

question: Which of these personal items must kitchen staff take off before they start working?

options.A: Non-slip kitchen shoes
options.B: Hairnets and caps
options.C: Clean cotton aprons
options.D: Rings and wristwatches

explanation: Rings and watches trap dirt and hidden bacteria that are tough to wash away. Taking them off keeps the kitchen truly clean! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h4)

question: A kitchen worker comes in with a sudden case of watery diarrhea and a mild fever. What should be done immediately?

options.A: Ask them to wash dishes with hot water instead
options.B: Take them off food handling duties right away
options.C: Tell them to swallow an anti-diarrhea drug and keep working
options.D: Let them work as long as they wear two pairs of gloves

explanation: Any worker showing signs of a tummy bug must be kept away from food immediately to stop germs from spreading to everyone else. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h4)

question: What is the name of the temperature zone where bacteria grow and multiply the fastest?

options.C: 0°C to 4°C
options.D: 5°C to 60°C

explanation: The 'danger zone' is between 5°C and 60°C. In this warmth, bacteria can double in number in just twenty minutes! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h5)

question: Why must raw meat always go on the lowest shelf of the fridge?

options.A: So it is faster for the cooks to grab
options.B: To keep it closest to the fridge cooling fan
options.C: To stop meat juices from dripping onto other foods below
options.D: Because raw meat likes warmer spots than veggies

explanation: Gravity is sneaky! If raw meat drips onto ready-to-eat foods below it, it spreads harmful germs. Always keep raw meat at the bottom. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h5)

question: What is the main difference between cleaning and sanitizing?

options.A: Cleaning uses chemicals, while sanitizing uses only plain water
options.B: Cleaning washes away visible dirt, while sanitizing brings germs down to a safe level
options.C: Cleaning kills bacteria, while sanitizing removes grease
options.D: Cleaning is done daily, while sanitizing is done once a year

explanation: Think of cleaning as washing away the physical mess (like grease and crumbs), while sanitizing uses heat or chemicals to knock out invisible germs. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h6)

question: Why are rats, mice, and insects so dangerous around a kitchen?

options.A: They make food lose its vitamins too quickly
options.B: They make annoying noises that disturb staff and guests
options.C: They eat too much food and increase restaurant bills
options.D: They carry and spread dangerous germs on their bodies and waste

explanation: Pests carry loads of bacteria, viruses, and parasites. When they crawl over surfaces, they leave behind invisible pathogens that can make people sick. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h6)

question: Which government agency is mainly responsible for regulating food safety and standards in Nigeria?

options.A: Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC)
options.B: Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN)
options.C: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)
options.D: Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC)

explanation: NAFDAC is our national watchdog ensuring that food, drugs, and chemicals sold in Nigeria are safe for everyone. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h7)

question: Why do food workers in Nigeria need a mandatory medical certificate?

options.A: To prove they are free from infectious diseases before handling food
options.B: To test how well they can cook local dishes
options.C: To help local government offices generate revenue
options.D: To figure out the right salary level for kitchen staff

explanation: Medical checks ensure that kitchen staff aren't carrying hidden infections that could easily spread to the meals they prepare. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h7)

question: What is the best way to tell if a food safety training program actually worked?

options.A: Watching to see if workers practice safe habits on the kitchen floor
options.B: Making sure everyone memorized the manual word-for-word
options.C: Calculating how much money was spent on the workshop
options.D: Checking that everyone sat through every minute of the lecture

explanation: Real learning shows in daily habits! True success is when staff actually use what they learned while cooking and cleaning. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h8)

question: Why is interactive training better for food workers than just reading a textbook?

options.A: Textbooks are too costly for big restaurant teams
options.B: Reading books is strictly banned in commercial kitchens
options.C: Adults learn and remember better through hands-on practice and real examples
options.D: Practical training means workers don't need health certificates

explanation: We learn best by doing! Hands-on practice helps us understand safety rules better and remember them when it counts. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h8)

question: Who counts as a food handler in public health?

options.A: Only certified chefs working in large hotel kitchens
options.B: Health inspectors who visit restaurants once a year
options.C: Factory workers who manufacture food packaging materials
options.D: Anyone who touches food, equipment, or food contact surfaces

explanation: Anyone who comes into direct contact with food, cooking tools, or preparation surfaces during their work is considered a food handler. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h1)

question: Why is keeping a close eye on food handlers such a big deal for public health?

options.A: It guarantees that restaurants make a high financial profit
options.B: It reduces the amount of spoiled food thrown away in kitchens
options.C: It speeds up the time it takes to cook meals for customers
options.D: It stops infected workers from causing widespread foodborne illness outbreaks

explanation: Because food handlers prepare meals for many people, proper oversight stops germs from spreading quickly to the public. Excellent thinking! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h1)

question: What do we mean by cross-contamination in the kitchen?

options.A: The transfer of harmful germs from raw food to ready-to-eat food
options.B: Mixing different brands of cooking oil together in a pot
options.C: Cooking food at a temperature that is far too high
options.D: Storing dry goods in the same room as cleaning chemicals

explanation: Cross-contamination happens when germs move from raw items (like meat) onto foods that won't be cooked any further. Keep up the great work! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h2)

question: A cook uses the same chopping board for raw chicken and fresh tomatoes without washing it first. What just happened?

options.A: Chemical toxicity
options.B: Physical adulteration
options.C: Cross-contamination
options.D: Thermal destruction

explanation: Using dirty equipment between raw meat and fresh veggies easily transfers bacteria from one to the other. Spot on! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h2)

question: How long should a food handler scrub their hands with soap and water?

options.A: As long as 5 minutes
options.B: Up to 2 minutes
options.C: Exactly 5 seconds
options.D: At least 20 seconds

explanation: Scrubbing with soap for a minimum of 20 seconds is the magic number to properly wash away germs on the skin. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h3)

question: Why must a food handler with a finger cut wear a brightly colored waterproof bandage?

options.A: To prevent the bandage from absorbing water in the sink
options.B: To make it easily visible if it falls off into the food
options.C: To speed up the healing process of the skin wound
options.D: To hide the injury from customers who might feel uncomfortable

explanation: Bright waterproof plasters make it super easy to spot and retrieve the bandage if it accidentally drops into a meal. Smart, right? [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h3)

question: Which of these symptoms means a food handler needs to step away from work right away?

options.A: A slight muscular leg cramp
options.B: Chronic dry scalp dandruff
options.C: Mild seasonal allergies
options.D: Diarrhea and vomiting

explanation: Tummy troubles like diarrhea and vomiting point to an active infection that can easily contaminate food. Safety first! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h4)

question: What is the main reason for routine health checkups before hiring food handlers?

options.A: To detect communicable diseases before workers start preparing food
options.B: To assess how well workers can handle high-stress kitchen environments
options.C: To determine the correct salary grade for each new kitchen employee
options.D: To test the physical strength and endurance of kitchen staff

explanation: Screenings catch infectious illnesses early so sick or asymptomatic workers don't spread germs to customers. Brilliant! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h4)

question: Why are unannounced kitchen inspections usually better than scheduled visits?

options.A: They ensure that all food items are cooked at very high heat
options.B: They give the kitchen staff time to hide dirty equipment
options.C: They reduce the amount of paperwork the supervisor must complete
options.D: They show normal, everyday kitchen habits and practices

explanation: Surprise checks mean staff can't just clean up and put on a show temporarily for the inspector. Makes total sense! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT something a food safety supervisor needs to check?

options.A: Observing proper handwashing compliance
options.B: Monitoring refrigerator and freezer temperatures
options.C: Checking employee credit history records
options.D: Inspecting the safe storage of raw and cooked food

explanation: An employee's financial history has nothing to do with food safety! Inspections focus purely on hygiene and temperature control. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h5)

question: Which Nigerian agency is well known for regulating food and drug safety?

options.A: JAMB
options.B: NAFDAC
options.C: NYSC
options.D: FRSC

explanation: NAFDAC (National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control) is our main regulatory body for food and drugs in Nigeria. Proudly Nigerian nursing knowledge! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h6)

question: What is the main goal of public health laws for food businesses?

options.A: To collect high taxes from commercial food business owners
options.B: To limit the number of small restaurants operating in local communities
options.C: To standardize recipe ingredients across different cultural restaurants
options.D: To establish minimum safety and sanitation rules that protect the public

explanation: Public health rules set clear hygiene and facility standards to prevent widespread food poisoning. You've got this down! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h6)

question: Why is interactive training better than just handing out printed rulebooks to food handlers?

options.A: It guarantees that workers will pass a written government exam
options.B: It eliminates the need for any future workplace supervision
options.C: It helps workers understand the practical reasons behind safety habits
options.D: It ensures that workers spend less time working in the kitchen

explanation: Demonstrations connect dry rules to real-life risks, making it much easier for staff to actually change their habits. Awesome! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h7)

question: Some food handlers are struggling with hygiene rules because they find English difficult. What should the nurse supervisor do?

options.A: Stop doing hygiene training and rely only on surprise inspections
options.B: Punish the workers for failing to read the English instruction manual
options.C: Conduct training sessions using the local language and visual demonstrations
options.D: Report the workers to the police for breaking environmental laws

explanation: Adapting how you teach to match your audience ensures everyone understands these life-saving safety practices. Great clinical judgment! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h7)

question: Which record is a must-have for a food business during health checks?

options.A: Supplier private bank statements
options.B: Refrigerator temperature logs
options.C: Daily employee social media posts
options.D: Customer personal phone numbers

explanation: Temperature logs prove that perishable foods stayed safely out of the bacterial danger zone over time. You're flying through these! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h8)

question: An inspector visits a restaurant and finds rotten food right next to fresh vegetables. What is the best immediate action?

options.A: Issue a corrective action notice and supervise the disposal of the spoiled food
options.B: Ask the customers dining in the restaurant to pay half price
options.C: Promote the head chef to a higher managerial position for honesty
options.D: Ignore the violation as long as the kitchen floor looks clean

explanation: Bad food must be tossed out immediately, and the violation documented to keep the public safe. Fantastic finish! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h8)

question: As a nurse, what is one of your main roles when it comes to nutrition and diet therapy?

options.A: Translating nutrition therapy into practical everyday habits for patients
options.B: Writing the definitive medical nutrition prescription for the hospital kitchen
options.C: Designing institutional food service menus for surgical wards
options.D: Diagnosing rare nutritional deficiencies using laboratory blood work

explanation: You are the vital link between doctor's orders and real life! Your job is to help patients take clinical nutrition advice and fit it smoothly into their daily meals and lifestyle. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T008#GNS227_U7_T008_h1)

question: Why must you always keep a patient's culture and pocket (financial status) in mind when giving dietary advice?

options.A: Hospital accreditation agencies legally mandate recording patient income
options.B: Low-income patients are exempt from following strict therapeutic diets
options.C: Dietary plans that ignore these factors are much less likely to be followed
options.D: Cultural foods always contain hidden chemicals that alter blood test results

explanation: If you recommend foreign foods or things they cannot afford to buy in the market, they simply won't do it. Tailor your advice to what is accessible and familiar to them! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T008#GNS227_U7_T008_h1)

question: What is the main reason we advise patients with high blood pressure to cut down on salt (sodium)?

options.A: To prevent the rapid digestion of dietary carbohydrates
options.B: To reduce intravascular volume and vascular resistance
options.C: To increase total body serum potassium levels
options.D: To stimulate increased red blood cell production

explanation: Salt makes the body hold onto water. Less salt means less fluid volume in the blood vessels, which lowers the pressure pushing against their walls. Easy and logical! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T008#GNS227_U7_T008_h2)

question: A patient asks which eating pattern is best for keeping their blood pressure in check. What should you tell them?

options.A: A high-protein, zero-fiber carnivore diet to preserve muscle mass
options.B: A clear liquid diet to cleanse the digestive and circulatory systems
options.C: A strict low-carbohydrate ketogenic diet with high saturated fats
options.D: The DASH diet rich in fruits, vegetables, and low-fat dairy

explanation: The DASH diet (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) is a classic winner! It packs in potassium, calcium, and fiber from whole foods to naturally bring pressure down. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T008#GNS227_U7_T008_h2)

question: How does eating plenty of fiber help a patient managing diabetes mellitus?

options.A: By slowing down the absorption of carbohydrates in the gut
options.B: By directly acting as a substitute for pancreatic insulin
options.C: By accelerating the breakdown of simple sugars in the stomach
options.D: By entirely blocking the digestion of dietary fats

explanation: Fiber acts like a speed bump in the digestive tract, slowing down how fast sugar enters the bloodstream and preventing those sudden spikes after a meal. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T008#GNS227_U7_T008_h3)

question: Why is keeping a consistent meal schedule so important for a diabetic patient taking insulin?

options.A: To match the timing of food intake with peak insulin action and prevent low blood sugar
options.B: To ensure the digestive enzymes are secreted in exact equal amounts daily
options.C: To guarantee that the liver stores excess fat in safe tissue compartments
options.D: To prevent the patient from experiencing chronic kidney failure symptoms

explanation: When insulin is active in the body but food is delayed, blood sugar can crash dangerously low (hypoglycemia). Regular meals keep them safe and balanced. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T008#GNS227_U7_T008_h3)

question: In chronic kidney disease, why do we need to restrict foods that are high in phosphorus?

options.A: To stop the sudden accumulation of excess stomach acid
options.B: To stimulate healthy red blood cell production in the bone marrow
options.C: To reduce the frequency of painful urinary tract infections
options.D: To prevent bone disease and dangerous vascular calcification

explanation: Failing kidneys struggle to clear phosphorus. Excess phosphorus steals calcium from the bones and hardens blood vessels, which spells trouble for the heart. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T008#GNS227_U7_T008_h4)

question: A patient with advanced kidney disease has high potassium levels in their blood. Which local fruit should you advise them to limit?

options.A: Plain clear water and herbal tea
options.B: Unsalted butter and cooking oils
options.C: Ripe bananas and fresh oranges
options.D: White refined flour and table sugar

explanation: Bananas and oranges are loaded with potassium! When the kidneys aren't working well, extra potassium can cause dangerous heart rhythm problems. Always good to know. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T008#GNS227_U7_T008_h4)

question: What is the absolute golden rule of diet therapy for a patient diagnosed with celiac disease?

options.A: Complete avoidance of all dairy and lactose products
options.B: A temporary increase in high-fiber whole grains
options.C: Lifelong strict elimination of dietary gluten
options.D: A high-sodium diet to prevent dehydration

explanation: Celiac disease triggers an immune reaction against gluten that damages the gut. Cutting out gluten completely is the only way the intestines can heal and stay healthy. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T008#GNS227_U7_T008_h5)

question: Why is a low-residue (low-fiber, easy-to-digest) diet often given during a flare-up of inflammatory bowel disease?

options.A: To prevent the development of high blood pressure and fluid retention
options.B: To provide extra protein necessary for healing surgical incisions
options.C: To minimize mechanical irritation and reduce the workload on the inflamed bowel
options.D: To stimulate rapid weight loss and reduce overall body fat percentage

explanation: Think of it as giving the gut a gentle break. Low-residue foods leave very little waste behind, letting the sore, inflamed intestines rest and recover. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T008#GNS227_U7_T008_h5)

question: Which of these is a common blood test result used to check a patient's nutritional status?

options.A: Capillary blood pressure
options.B: Total daily step count
options.C: Resting heart rate
options.D: Serum albumin

explanation: Serum albumin is a classic protein marker in the blood that nurses and doctors look at to check if a patient is getting enough building blocks for their body. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T008#GNS227_U7_T008_h6)

question: Why is it smart to check a patient's readiness to change before you start teaching them complex diet plans?

options.A: It is required by law to document patient compliance before prescribing medication
options.B: It identifies which specific food allergies the patient was born with
options.C: It prevents wasting time on complex meal plans if the patient is not yet willing to alter habits
options.D: It determines the exact amount of daily calories the patient's kidneys can filter

explanation: Education only lands when someone is ready to listen. If a patient is still in denial about their diagnosis, pushing a strict meal plan right away won't work. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T008#GNS227_U7_T008_h6)

question: What is the main goal of using the 'teach-back' method when educating a patient?

options.A: To ensure the physician documented the correct diagnosis in the chart
options.B: To confirm that the patient truly understands the instructions in their own words
options.C: To test the patient's long-term memory after a neurological injury
options.D: To give the nurse a break from talking during the clinical consultation

explanation: Instead of asking 'Do you understand?' (where they'll just say yes), teach-back has them explain it back to you. It catches any misunderstandings instantly! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T008#GNS227_U7_T008_h7)

question: A patient says they can't follow their diabetic meal plan because fresh veggies are too expensive in their area. What is your best first nursing move?

options.A: Ignore the comment and repeat the original dietary brochure word for word
options.B: Advise the patient to stop eating vegetables entirely and take vitamin pills
options.C: Explore affordable alternatives like frozen or canned vegetables and consult social work
options.D: Tell the patient that buying fresh vegetables is mandatory for survival

explanation: Be a problem solver! Listen to their financial hurdles and help them find budget-friendly swaps so they can still eat healthy without breaking the bank. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T008#GNS227_U7_T008_h7)

question: What happens to the body's energy and protein needs after surgery?

options.A: They remain exactly the same as pre-surgery levels
options.B: They decrease because the patient is resting in bed
options.C: They increase due to tissue trauma and healing
options.D: They stop completely until solid food is tolerated

explanation: Great job! Surgery causes physical stress, so the body needs extra energy and protein to heal the tissues properly. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h1)

question: Why is checking for malnutrition important before a patient goes for surgery?

options.A: It shortens the time the patient spends in the recovery room
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any intravenous fluids
options.C: It ensures the patient will never feel nauseated after waking up
options.D: It helps the body withstand surgical stress and prevents complications

explanation: Spot on! Well-nourished patients handle the stress of an operation much better and have a lower risk of infections. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h1)

question: Which blood test is commonly checked to assess a patient's nutrition before surgery?

options.A: Serum albumin
options.B: Red blood cell count
options.C: Blood glucose
options.D: Platelet count

explanation: You got it! Serum albumin is a classic protein marker we use to check a surgical patient's nutritional reserves. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h2)

question: Why might a patient be given a carbohydrate drink up to two hours before surgery?

options.A: To replace the need for intravenous fluids during the operation
options.B: To reduce insulin resistance and postoperative discomfort
options.C: To prevent the patient from experiencing surgical site infections
options.D: To completely fill the stomach so the patient feels full

explanation: Correct! Giving carbs before surgery helps calm fasting stress, keeps insulin working well, and cuts down on post-surgery nausea. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h2)

question: Which hormones are mainly responsible for breaking down fat and muscle during the stress of surgery?

options.A: Cortisol and glucagon
options.B: Antidiuretic hormone
options.C: Insulin and estrogen
options.D: Thyroid stimulating hormone

explanation: Well done! Stress hormones like cortisol and glucagon shoot up during surgery to quickly mobilize energy for the body. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h3)

question: Why is getting enough protein so crucial during the body's recovery phase after surgery?

options.A: It acts as a mild pain reliever for the surgical wound
options.B: It prevents the patient from experiencing low blood pressure
options.C: It stops the endocrine system from releasing stress hormones
options.D: It provides the amino acids needed to rebuild broken down muscle and repair incisions

explanation: Right! Protein supplies the building blocks (amino acids) needed to close wounds and rebuild tissues after the body has broken them down. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h3)

question: When do modern recovery guidelines generally suggest starting food by mouth after surgery?

options.A: Only after 48 hours of complete fasting
options.B: Within hours of waking from anesthesia
options.C: After waiting for active bowel sounds
options.D: Only after the patient passes flatus

explanation: Spot on! Feeding patients early is safe and actually helps their bowels wake up faster than starving them for days. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h4)

question: A patient eating a full liquid diet after surgery suddenly gets severe stomach cramps and vomits. What should you do first?

options.A: Immediately upgrade the diet to solid foods
options.B: Encourage the patient to finish the meal quickly
options.C: Document the findings and ignore the symptoms
options.D: Pause the feeding and notify the surgical team

explanation: Correct! Cramping and vomiting mean the gut isn't ready yet. We need to stop the feeding and let the doctor know. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h4)

question: Why is feeding through the gut (enteral nutrition) usually preferred over drips (parenteral nutrition) for surgical patients?

options.A: It preserves gut immune function and carries fewer infectious risks
options.B: It is absorbed much faster than intravenous fluids
options.C: It bypasses the digestive system entirely
options.D: It can be administered without any medical equipment

explanation: You got it! Using the natural digestive tract keeps the gut healthy and avoids the high infection risks that come with central lines. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h5)

question: When is total parenteral nutrition (feeding directly into the veins) specifically needed?

options.A: When the gastrointestinal tract is completely non-functional or obstructed
options.B: When the patient simply dislikes the taste of hospital food
options.C: When the patient is able to swallow clear liquids
options.D: When the surgery only involved a minor skin biopsy

explanation: Spot on! We only use IV nutrition when the gut cannot work or is blocked, since it bypasses the digestive system completely. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h5)

question: What is dumping syndrome?

options.A: An allergic reaction to intravenous protein solutions
options.B: Rapid emptying of stomach contents into the small intestine causing dizziness and cramps
options.C: The inability of the kidneys to filter waste products after major surgery
options.D: The total stoppage of bowel movements for over a week

explanation: Well done! Dumping syndrome happens when food rushes too fast from a smaller stomach into the small intestine, making the patient feel dizzy and cramped. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h6)

question: Why are bariatric (weight-loss) surgery patients told not to drink fluids at the same time they eat solid meals?

options.A: To prevent the stomach from overfilling and to avoid triggering dumping syndrome
options.B: To prevent the absorption of any vitamins or minerals
options.C: To make digestion take as long as humanly possible
options.D: To ensure they lose as much water weight as possible

explanation: Correct! Drinking water with meals washes the food through a tiny stomach pouch too quickly, causing discomfort and cramping. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h6)

question: Which vitamin is especially important for building collagen during long-term wound healing?

options.A: Vitamin B12
options.B: Vitamin C
options.C: Vitamin K
options.D: Vitamin D

explanation: You nailed it! Vitamin C is key for making collagen, which acts like glue to heal surgical cuts. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h7)

question: Why does recovery from surgery continue for weeks or months after the skin stitches are removed?

options.A: Patients are usually restricted to liquid diets for six months
options.B: Deep internal tissues take weeks to months to regain full tensile strength
options.C: External healing is just a cosmetic illusion with no internal progress
options.D: The body stops absorbing any nutrients once the skin closes

explanation: Spot on! Even though the outside skin looks fine, the deeper muscles and tissues take much longer to get their full strength back. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h7)

question: What is a very common side effect of post-surgical pain medications that ruins a patient's appetite?

options.A: High fever
options.B: Rapid hair growth
options.C: Increased muscle mass
options.D: Constipation

explanation: Right! Pain medicines like opioids slow down the bowels, causing stubborn constipation that kills appetite and brings on nausea. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h8)

question: A postoperative patient refuses to eat because food always brings severe belly pain and nausea. What is your best nursing action?

options.A: Administer prescribed pain and anti-nausea medications thirty minutes before the next meal
options.B: Remove all food trays permanently and start total parenteral nutrition
options.C: Force the patient to finish the entire meal tray immediately
options.D: Tell the patient that eating is mandatory for legal discharge

explanation: Brilliant! Managing pain and nausea before mealtime makes eating comfortable so the patient can actually get their nutrition. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h8)

question: Which main nerve links the gastrointestinal tract directly to the brain?

options.A: The phrenic nerve
options.B: The trigeminal nerve
options.C: The vagus nerve
options.D: The sciatic nerve

explanation: Spot on! The vagus nerve is the primary communication highway connecting your gut and your brain. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h1)

question: Why is the gut often called our second brain regarding mood?

options.A: It prevents all forms of physical inflammation
options.B: It directly digests complex psychiatric medications
options.C: It completely replaces the function of the brain
options.D: It produces most of the body's serotonin supply

explanation: Correct! Specialized cells and microbes in your gut manufacture a large share of your body's serotonin, directly influencing your mood. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h1)

question: How does chronic psychological stress typically affect food cravings?

options.A: It increases a natural desire for raw vegetables and water
options.B: It raises cortisol and triggers cravings for fatty, sugary foods
options.C: It forces the digestive system to absorb fewer total calories
options.D: It completely stops the body from digesting any proteins

explanation: You got it! High cortisol from stress tricks the brain into seeking out dense, comforting, high-calorie foods for quick energy. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h2)

question: A patient with severe schizophrenia is losing weight because they never cook or buy groceries. What is the main reason for this?

options.A: A physical inability to chew or swallow solid food
options.B: An allergic reaction to standard grocery store items
options.C: Negative symptoms like apathy and lack of drive
options.D: A deliberate choice to fast for religious reasons

explanation: Well done! Negative symptoms such as avolition can rob patients of the motivation needed to plan and execute daily tasks like cooking. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h2)

question: Which group of psychiatric drugs is most famous for causing rapid weight gain?

options.A: Short-acting sleeping tablets
options.B: Standard over-the-counter vitamins
options.C: Mild herbal anxiety supplements
options.D: Second-generation antipsychotics

explanation: Correct! These medications heavily impact metabolism and appetite control, often leading to rapid weight gain. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h3)

question: Why do patients taking lithium need careful guidance about their salt and water intake?

options.A: Salt completely destroys the chemical structure of the lithium pill
options.B: Lithium alters fluid balance and can easily reach toxic levels if hydration shifts
options.C: Water causes lithium to instantly evaporate inside the human stomach
options.D: Patients on lithium lose all sense of taste for salty foods

explanation: Spot on! Lithium handles similarly to sodium in the kidneys, so dehydration or sudden salt changes can dangerously spike drug levels. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h3)

question: Which lab tests are most important when starting a patient on an antipsychotic known for metabolic side effects?

options.A: Direct measurement of brain wave activity
options.B: Fasting blood glucose and lipid profile
options.C: Routine throat swab for bacterial culture
options.D: Complete stool analysis for parasites

explanation: Correct! Because these drugs can disrupt blood sugar and fats, keeping an eye on glucose and lipid levels is essential. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h4)

question: A depressed patient has lost ten pounds, looks pale, and is fatigued. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Assume the weight loss is normal for depression and take no action
options.B: Perform a comprehensive nutritional assessment including a diet history and labs
options.C: Recommend an intense physical fitness gym membership to build muscle
options.D: Tell the patient to immediately start eating three large meals a day

explanation: Well done! A structured assessment helps us uncover specific nutritional deficits and physical health risks. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h4)

question: Why do we generally recommend complex carbohydrates over simple sugars for psychiatric patients?

options.A: They prevent the dramatic energy crashes that can worsen mood swings
options.B: They taste much sweeter and satisfy cravings instantly
options.C: They require no digestion and enter the bloodstream immediately
options.D: They completely cure all forms of clinical depression overnight

explanation: Correct! Complex carbs digest slowly, keeping blood sugar and energy levels stable throughout the day. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h5)

question: What common physical issue can mild dehydration often mimic in a psychiatric patient?

options.A: Rapid hair loss and brittle fingernails
options.B: Sudden weight gain and high blood pressure
options.C: Complete loss of the sense of hearing
options.D: Fatigue, confusion, and worsening anxiety

explanation: Spot on! Not drinking enough water frequently presents as brain fog, tiredness, and heightened nervous tension. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h5)

question: Which food must be strictly avoided by a patient taking a Monoamine Oxidase Inhibitor (MAOI)?

options.A: Fresh green leafy vegetables
options.B: Plain boiled white rice
options.C: Pasteurized cow's milk
options.D: Aged cheeses and cured meats

explanation: You got it! These foods are high in tyramine, which can trigger a dangerous, life-threatening spike in blood pressure when combined with MAOIs. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h6)

question: What is the main goal of recommending an anti-inflammatory diet, like the Mediterranean diet, in psychiatric care?

options.A: To force the body to rapidly lose large amounts of water weight
options.B: To cure genetic disorders within a few weeks of starting
options.C: To completely eliminate the need for any prescription medications
options.D: To reduce systemic inflammation that negatively impacts brain function

explanation: Correct! Lowering bodily inflammation helps support optimal brain health and can ease depressive symptoms. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h6)

question: What is a practical, budget-friendly nursing tip for a patient who cannot afford fresh vegetables?

options.A: Advise them to forage for wild plants in local public parks
options.B: Telling them to skip vegetables entirely until they find more money
options.C: Suggesting nutritious frozen vegetables or rinsed canned options
options.D: Insisting they only buy organic produce from specialty markets

explanation: Well done! Frozen and canned veggies are affordable, last longer, and still offer great nutrition when money is tight. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to healthy eating for vulnerable psychiatric patients?

options.A: An overabundance of free local community gardens
options.B: Financial poverty and limited access to grocery stores
options.C: Living in an area classified as a food desert
options.D: Cognitive impairment affecting meal preparation

explanation: Spot on! Poverty and poor access are major hurdles, whereas having plenty of community gardens would actually help people get fresh food. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h7)

question: Why is the nurse considered the central link in nutritional care for psychiatric patients?

options.A: They hold the legal authority to prescribe all specialized diets
options.B: They are the only team members trained in human biology
options.C: They dictate what medications the psychiatrist must order
options.D: They spend the most time with the patient and monitor daily habits

explanation: Correct! Because nurses are constantly around patients, they are in the best position to track real-time food intake and side effects. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h8)

question: A patient on a new psychiatric drug is refusing to eat due to severe dry mouth. Who should the nurse consult first?

options.A: The medical records coding and billing department
options.B: The registered dietitian and the prescribing psychiatrist
options.C: The hospital maintenance and facility management team
options.D: The security personnel assigned to the psychiatric unit

explanation: You got it! A dietitian can help modify food textures for dry mouth, while the psychiatrist can review the medication dosage. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h8)

question: What is the main goal of teaching pregnant mothers about good nutrition during antenatal care?

options.A: To help the mother lose weight during the first trimester
options.B: To guarantee a completely painless labor and delivery
options.C: To eliminate the need for routine blood pressure checks
options.D: To prevent low birth weight and support fetal development

explanation: You've got this! Proper nutrition is key to helping the baby grow strong and healthy while keeping the mother in great shape throughout her pregnancy. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T011#GNS227_U7_T011_h1)

question: Why is it so important for a nurse to check a pregnant patient's diet early on?

options.A: It determines the exact date of conception
options.B: It replaces the need for standard laboratory blood tests
options.C: It allows for the early identification and correction of nutrient deficits
options.D: It stops gestational diabetes from ever developing

explanation: Spotting nutritional gaps early helps you stop issues like tiredness or baby growth delays before they become serious. Great nursing insight! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T011#GNS227_U7_T011_h1)

question: About how much does a normal pregnant woman's total blood volume increase?

options.A: 5 percent
options.B: 100 percent
options.C: 10 percent
options.D: 50 percent

explanation: Amazing right? The body ramps up blood volume by about half to care for both the mother and the growing baby. That's why iron and fluids are so crucial! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T011#GNS227_U7_T011_h2)

question: During which part of pregnancy do a mother's daily food energy (calorie) needs go up the most?

options.A: Third trimester
options.B: The first two weeks postpartum
options.C: During active labor
options.D: First trimester

explanation: As the baby gets bigger towards the end of pregnancy, calorie needs peak—demanding extra energy to cross the finish line! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T011#GNS227_U7_T011_h2)

question: What is the main reason we give folic acid supplements in early pregnancy?

options.A: To stop maternal gestational hypertension
options.B: To prevent postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: To prevent neural tube defects
options.D: To increase daily breast milk production

explanation: Folic acid is a tiny pill with a huge job! It protects the baby's developing brain and spine right from the very start. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T011#GNS227_U7_T011_h3)

question: A patient asks why she needs extra iron when her test shows mild anemia. What is your best reply?

options.A: Your blood volume increases greatly, and iron helps build the extra hemoglobin needed.
options.B: Iron tablets replace the calories you lose from not eating enough protein.
options.C: Iron prevents the baby from developing weak bones and teeth.
options.D: Extra iron is only given to stop morning sickness in the first trimester.

explanation: Because her blood volume stretches so much, the blood gets diluted. Extra iron helps her body build all those extra red blood cells she needs! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T011#GNS227_U7_T011_h3)

question: What is a great food tip for a mum dealing with early morning sickness?

options.A: Consuming a large, high-fat breakfast immediately upon waking
options.B: Drinking two large glasses of citrus juice on an empty stomach
options.C: Eating small, dry carbohydrate snacks like crackers before getting out of bed
options.D: Restricting all fluid intake throughout the entire day

explanation: Dry snacks help settle a restless morning tummy and gently boost blood sugar without triggering nausea. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T011#GNS227_U7_T011_h4)

question: A patient with gestational diabetes asks what diet changes to make. What should you suggest?

options.A: Focus on complex carbohydrates, increase fiber, and eat evenly spaced meals
options.B: Avoid all proteins and eat only sugary fruits for energy
options.C: Eliminate all forms of food and rely only on protein shakes
options.D: Eat large meals twice a day to reduce insulin spikes

explanation: Keeping blood sugar stable is all about steady, fiber-rich meals that digest slowly rather than spiking glucose all at once. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T011#GNS227_U7_T011_h4)

question: Which fish should pregnant women avoid because of the risk of harming the baby's nervous system?

options.A: Low-fat white fish like tilapia and cod
options.B: Canned tuna in small weekly portions
options.C: Freshwater fish caught in local rivers
options.D: High-mercury fish like swordfish and shark

explanation: Fish like swordfish and shark carry higher mercury levels which can cross the placenta, so it's safest for mums to steer clear! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T011#GNS227_U7_T011_h5)

question: Why are pregnant women more easily infected by bugs like listeriosis from unpasteurized foods?

options.A: Their high blood volume washes bacteria directly into the placenta
options.B: They produce more stomach acid which attracts bacteria
options.C: Their cell-mediated immune system is naturally suppressed during pregnancy
options.D: Their liver function slows down and cannot filter toxins

explanation: Nature gently lowers the immune response so the body accepts the baby, but it also means food safety is extra important during pregnancy. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T011#GNS227_U7_T011_h5)

question: Roughly how many extra daily calories does a breastfeeding mother need?

options.A: 1000 to 1200 kilocalories
options.B: Zero extra calories are needed
options.C: 450 to 500 kilocalories
options.D: 100 to 150 kilocalories

explanation: Making breast milk takes a lot of body power! Mums actually need even more extra energy daily while breastfeeding than they did while pregnant. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T011#GNS227_U7_T011_h6)

question: Why should you advise a new mother NOT to start a crash weight-loss diet right after delivery while breastfeeding?

options.A: It can decrease milk volume and deplete her own nutrient stores
options.B: It will cause the baby to develop an allergy to breast milk
options.C: It stops the uterus from shrinking back to normal size
options.D: It causes immediate postpartum depression

explanation: Her body needs good nourishment to recover from childbirth and keep up a healthy milk supply for her baby. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T011#GNS227_U7_T011_h6)

question: What is the best approach when advising a pregnant mum on a tight budget about her diet?

options.A: Insisting that she must purchase organic foods to have a healthy baby
options.B: Suggesting affordable, locally available food alternatives that meet her nutritional needs
options.C: Skipping dietary counseling because poverty makes nutrition impossible to change
options.D: Telling her to buy expensive imported supplements from specialized pharmacies

explanation: Great nursing care is practical and real! Always guide patients toward nourishing, budget-friendly local foods they can actually access. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T011#GNS227_U7_T011_h7)

question: Which communication trick helps a nurse truly understand what a patient normally eats?

options.A: Assuming all patients eat the same traditional hospital diet
options.B: Handing out a pamphlet and asking if they can read
options.C: Reading a strict list of forbidden foods and waiting for agreement
options.D: Asking open-ended questions about what foods the patient eats at home

explanation: Open-ended questions like 'Tell me what you usually eat in a day' invite honest chats and help you give advice that fits their real life. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T011#GNS227_U7_T011_h7)

question: What makes paediatric nutrition different from adult nutrition?

options.A: Reducing total daily caloric intake
options.B: Preventing lifestyle diseases like hypertension
options.C: Supporting rapid growth and organ maturation
options.D: Maintaining a stable body weight over time

explanation: You've got this! Children grow fast and their organs are still developing, so they need special nutrients. Adults, on the other hand, mostly just need to maintain their weight. Keep up the great work! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h1)

question: Why is good nutrition during early childhood so important?

options.A: Deficits during this window can cause permanent stunting and brain damage
options.B: Young children have fully developed organs that process food slowly
options.C: It prevents the child from ever catching infections later in life
options.D: Children naturally require fewer nutrients than adults do

explanation: Think of early childhood as a critical construction phase. Missing key nutrients here can unfortunately lead to lasting effects on growth and brain development. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h1)

question: According to global health guidelines, how long should an infant be exclusively breastfed?

options.A: For the first six months of life
options.B: For the first three months only
options.C: Until the infant starts walking
options.D: Until the baby cuts their first tooth

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months gives babies the absolute best start, providing all the water, food, and immune protection they need! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h2)

question: What is a major advantage of breast milk over animal milk for a newborn?

options.A: It has a much higher concentration of heavy proteins
options.B: It contains protective antibodies that fight off infections
options.C: It requires no digestion by the infant's stomach
options.D: It stays fresh at room temperature for days

explanation: Breast milk is nature's vaccine! It's packed with antibodies that protect a newborn's delicate immune system against germs. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h2)

question: At what age should complementary foods be introduced to an infant?

options.A: At three months of age
options.B: At six months of age
options.C: At nine months of age
options.D: At one year of age

explanation: Around six months, breast milk alone can't keep up with the baby's growing iron and energy demands. That's when safe complementary foods come in! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h3)

question: A mother asks what food to first give her six-month-old. What is the best nurse response?

options.A: Cow milk straight from the carton to build strong bones
options.B: Clear vegetable broths with added table salt for taste
options.C: Sweetened fruit juices to encourage quick swallowing
options.D: Thick, nutrient-dense mashed foods like iron-fortified porridge or yam

explanation: First foods should be thick and rich in nutrients, especially iron, to match the rapid growth spurt of a six-month-old baby. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h3)

question: Why do toddlers often experience a sudden drop in appetite?

options.A: They naturally dislike the taste of home-cooked meals
options.B: Their physical growth rate slows down compared to infancy
options.C: Their digestive systems can no longer process solid food
options.D: They prefer playing rather than sitting down to eat

explanation: Don't worry if a toddler eats less! Their growth velocity slows down after year one, meaning they just don't need as many calories per kilo anymore. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h4)

question: What is a common pitfall parents fall into when a toddler's appetite drops?

options.A: Stopping all forms of milk consumption immediately
options.B: Giving the child adult-sized portions at every meal
options.C: Providing too many green leafy vegetables
options.D: Forcing food or offering constant sugary snacks

explanation: When toddlers eat less, worried parents sometimes force meals or hand over sugary snacks, which unfortunately leads to picky eating habits. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h4)

question: Why do adolescent girls need more iron in their diet?

options.A: To increase their overall body fat percentage
options.B: To prevent the onset of juvenile diabetes
options.C: To support rapid thickening of tooth enamel
options.D: To replace iron lost during monthly menstruation

explanation: Teens growing up face new changes; adolescent girls need extra iron to make up for what is lost during monthly periods and keep anaemia away. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h5)

question: Which factor most frequently disrupts healthy eating habits during adolescence?

options.A: An inability to digest complex carbohydrates
options.B: Peer pressure and preoccupation with body image
options.C: A natural biological loss of interest in eating
options.D: The complete disappearance of hunger cues

explanation: Teens care a lot about fitting in and body image. Peer pressure and media trends often push them toward skipping meals or strict dieting. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h5)

question: What does MUAC stand for in paediatric nutritional assessment?

options.A: Mid-Upper Arm Circumference
options.B: Minimum Urinary Acid Concentration
options.C: Mean Underweight Assessment Criteria
options.D: Maximum Upper Abdominal Capacity

explanation: MUAC is a super handy, quick measurement used by community nurses to screen children for acute malnutrition right on the spot! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h6)

question: Why is plotting a child's weight and height on a standard growth chart so important?

options.A: It replaces the need for any clinical examination by a doctor
options.B: It gives an exact prediction of the child's adult height
options.C: It proves whether the child has a genetic heart condition
options.D: It helps spot downward trends in growth before severe malnutrition appears

explanation: Growth charts let you catch tiny warning signs early. Spotting a drop in the weight curve early helps stop malnutrition before it gets severe. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h6)

question: Which clinical sign is most characteristic of kwashiorkor?

options.A: Severe muscle wasting with no body fat at all
options.B: Rapid overgrowth of the long bones
options.C: Generalized pitting edema and skin changes
options.D: An extremely high fever with sudden seizures

explanation: Kwashiorkor happens when a child lacks enough protein. A classic giveaway is swelling (edema) in the body and noticeable skin changes. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h7)

question: What is a major danger of a severe Vitamin A deficiency in young children?

options.A: Extreme weight gain and early childhood obesity
options.B: Permanent softening of the bones resembling rickets
options.C: Uncontrolled bleeding due to lack of blood clotting factors
options.D: Increased risk of severe infections like measles and blindness

explanation: Vitamin A is a hero for eye health and immunity. Without it, kids are much more vulnerable to serious infections like measles, plus vision problems. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h7)

question: Why should a nurse recommend locally available foods during dietary counselling?

options.A: It ensures the family can afford and sustain the dietary advice
options.B: Government policies ban the use of foreign food items
options.C: Local foods require no cooking or preparation time
options.D: Imported foods are always toxic to young children

explanation: Good nursing advice must be practical! Recommending local foods ensures the family can actually afford and keep up with the diet. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h8)

question: A mother feels defensive when asked about her child's diet. What approach should the nurse use?

options.A: Use open-ended, non-judgmental questions to explore current practices
options.B: Hand her a detailed textbook and ask her to read it alone
options.C: Report the mother immediately to the hospital social worker
options.D: Scold the mother so she takes the nutritional advice more seriously

explanation: Empathy goes a long way! Asking open, friendly questions builds trust so mothers feel safe sharing their true feeding challenges. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h8)

question: What is the main goal of taking a nutritional supplement?

options.A: To add extra dietary ingredients to a person's daily intake
options.B: To cure chronic infectious diseases overnight
options.C: To completely replace the need for eating solid foods
options.D: To act as a prescribed pharmaceutical medication

explanation: Supplements are meant to add to your normal meals, not replace them! They give your body a little extra boost of vitamins or minerals when needed. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T013#GNS227_U7_T013_h1)

question: Why should nurses always ask patients about any supplements they are taking?

options.A: Supplements are always provided free of charge by the hospital pharmacy
options.B: Doctors prescribe them for every single diagnosis upon admission
options.C: Patients often take them independently and they can impact overall health
options.D: Hospitals require patients to stop all eating and only take supplements

explanation: Many people buy and take supplements on their own without telling anyone. As a nurse, asking about them helps you keep an eye on everything entering the patient's body! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T013#GNS227_U7_T013_h1)

question: Which group of vitamins is known as fat-soluble?

options.A: Vitamins A, D, E, and K
options.B: Vitamin C and the B-complex group
options.C: Calcium, iron, and potassium
options.D: Amino acids and plant extracts

explanation: Think of vitamins A, D, E, and K as the ones that dissolve in fat and can hang out in our body's fatty tissues and liver for later use. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T013#GNS227_U7_T013_h2)

question: How are minerals fundamentally different from vitamins?

options.A: Minerals are only found in pills, while vitamins come from plants
options.B: Minerals are inorganic elements, whereas vitamins are organic compounds
options.C: Minerals provide energy calories, whereas vitamins do not
options.D: Minerals dissolve in fat, whereas vitamins dissolve in water

explanation: Minerals like iron and calcium come straight from the earth and water (inorganic), whereas vitamins are made by living things (organic). Easy to remember once you link minerals to rocks and soil! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T013#GNS227_U7_T013_h2)

question: Which supplement is given to pregnant women to help prevent neural tube defects?

options.A: Vitamin C
options.B: Potassium chloride
options.C: Zinc gluconate
options.D: Folic acid

explanation: Folic acid is a super important vitamin during early pregnancy. It helps the baby's brain and spinal cord develop properly. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T013#GNS227_U7_T013_h3)

question: A patient who eats a strict vegan diet and avoids all animal products is most at risk of lacking which nutrient?

options.A: Vitamin B12
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Vitamin A

explanation: Vitamin B12 is mostly found in animal foods like meat, eggs, and dairy. Strict vegans often need to take a supplement to keep their B12 levels healthy. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T013#GNS227_U7_T013_h3)

question: What is the most reliable way to check if a patient actually has a nutrient deficiency?

options.A: Asking the patient what they ate yesterday
options.B: Observing the color of the patient's skin
options.C: Laboratory blood tests
options.D: Checking the patient's blood pressure

explanation: Lab tests give us clear, factual proof of what's inside the patient's blood, helping us avoid guessing or giving supplements they don't need. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T013#GNS227_U7_T013_h4)

question: Why can it be tricky to diagnose a nutrition problem based only on general tiredness?

options.A: Patients always exaggerate how tired they feel
options.B: Fatigue can be caused by many non-nutritional health conditions
options.C: Nutrient deficiencies never cause tiredness or weakness
options.D: Fatigue only occurs when a person is completely dehydrated

explanation: Feeling tired is a sign of many things—like lack of sleep, stress, or an infection—not just poor food intake. We have to look at the whole picture! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T013#GNS227_U7_T013_h4)

question: Which type of vitamin can easily build up to toxic levels if taken in excess over time?

options.A: Water-soluble vitamins
options.B: Fat-soluble vitamins
options.C: Amino acid supplements
options.D: Plant-based minerals

explanation: Because fat-soluble vitamins get stored in body fat instead of being peed out quickly, taking too many of them over time can lead to a harmful buildup. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T013#GNS227_U7_T013_h5)

question: What is a major risk when a patient takes herbal supplements along with their regular prescription drugs?

options.A: Herbs always neutralize all side effects of drugs
options.B: Adverse drug-nutrient or herb-drug interactions
options.C: The prescription drugs will become completely odorless
options.D: The medications will instantly turn into sugar

explanation: Herbs are active chemicals too! When mixed with hospital drugs, they can sometimes clash, making the drugs too strong or blocking them from working. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T013#GNS227_U7_T013_h5)

question: What important advice should you give a patient who wants to start taking a daily multivitamin?

options.A: Taking five times the recommended dose will speed up healing
options.B: Natural supplements never interact with prescribed heart medications
options.C: Supplements do not replace the benefits of eating a balanced, whole-food diet
options.D: There is no need to tell the doctor about over-the-counter vitamins

explanation: Real, whole foods give our bodies natural fiber and nutrients that pills just cannot completely copy. Supplements are helpers, not food substitutes! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T013#GNS227_U7_T013_h6)

question: Which of these is a bad practice when choosing a nutritional supplement?

options.A: Following the recommended dosage instructions on the bottle
options.B: Ignoring product labels and ingredient lists completely
options.C: Buying products verified by independent quality testing
options.D: Checking with a healthcare provider before starting

explanation: Always read the label! Ignoring it means you might miss allergy warnings, wrong dosages, or hidden ingredients. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T013#GNS227_U7_T013_h6)

question: What is the main goal of taking a dietary supplement?

options.A: To completely replace regular hospital meals
options.B: To add extra nutrients to a person's diet
options.C: To cure chronic infectious diseases overnight
options.D: To serve as the main source of daily calories

explanation: Supplements are simply meant to top up the nutrients you might be missing from your regular meals. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h1)

question: Why shouldn't dietary supplements replace whole foods?

options.A: Supplements are always too expensive for ordinary patients to afford daily
options.B: Whole foods provide a complex balance of nutrients and fiber that isolated supplements lack
options.C: Conventional foods contain prescription drugs that supplements completely lack
options.D: The human digestive tract cannot absorb any chemical compound created in a laboratory

explanation: Real foods give you a rich mix of fiber and interacting nutrients that a single pill just can't copy. Balance is key! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h1)

question: Which agency is responsible for regulating food and dietary supplements in Nigeria?

options.A: FMOH
options.B: Standard Organisation of Nigeria
options.C: WHO
options.D: NAFDAC

explanation: NAFDAC is our local body that keeps us safe by regulating drugs, food, and supplements in Nigeria. Great to keep in mind for clinical practice! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h2)

question: What is the safest action for a nurse when a patient brings an unregistered herbal supplement to the ward?

options.A: Store the product in the nurse's station and prescribe it to other patients
options.B: Encourage the patient to double the normal dosage for faster healing results
options.C: Taste the liquid content first to verify if it contains real medicinal herbs
options.D: Advise the patient to avoid using it because safety and quality cannot be guaranteed

explanation: If it's unregistered, we can't vouch for its safety or purity. Always advise caution with unknown products! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h2)

question: Under which category of supplements is iron classified?

options.A: Enzyme
options.B: Vitamin
options.C: Mineral
options.D: Herb

explanation: Iron is a vital mineral our bodies need to build hemoglobin for red blood cells. Simple and classic nursing knowledge! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h3)

question: Why do people commonly take protein powder supplements?

options.A: To treat acute bacterial infections in the respiratory tract
options.B: To support muscle growth and repair after physical exercise
options.C: To permanently lower high blood pressure levels
options.D: To cure chronic iron-deficiency anemia quickly

explanation: Protein gives the body the building blocks (amino acids) it needs to repair and build up muscle tissue after a workout. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h3)

question: Which supplement is very important during early pregnancy to prevent neural tube defects?

options.A: Vitamin K
options.B: Potassium chloride
options.C: Magnesium sulfate
options.D: Folic acid

explanation: Folic acid is a prenatal superstar! It protects the baby's developing brain and spine in the early weeks. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h4)

question: Why should a nurse check lab results before encouraging a patient to take high-dose supplements?

options.A: To find out if the patient is allergic to plastic medicine bottles
options.B: To make sure the patient can afford the expensive brand names sold in pharmacies
options.C: To calculate the exact hospital bed tax for nutritional therapy
options.D: To confirm the specific nutrient deficiency rather than guessing based on general fatigue

explanation: We test to be sure what's actually lacking. Guessing can lead to wasting money or even vitamin toxicity! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h4)

question: Which type of vitamin is most likely to cause toxicity if taken in excess because they store up in body fat?

options.A: Amino acid supplements
options.B: Water-soluble vitamins
options.C: B-complex vitamins
options.D: Fat-soluble vitamins

explanation: Vitamins A, D, E, and K dissolve in fat and hang around in the body instead of being flushed out in urine. Too much of a good thing can be harmful! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h5)

question: A patient on warfarin for a heart condition starts taking a daily garlic supplement. What is the major concern here?

options.A: The combination can significantly increase the risk of bleeding
options.B: The warfarin will turn the garlic tablets into poison
options.C: The patient will develop severe vitamin C toxicity
options.D: The garlic will completely cure the heart condition overnight

explanation: Garlic naturally thins the blood a little. Combined with warfarin, it can dangerously boost the bleeding risk. Always screen for herbal-drug interactions! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h5)

question: Why do many patients forget to mention their herbal supplements during a medication history interview?

options.A: Herbal products dissolve instantly and leave no trace in the body
options.B: Hospital regulations strictly forbid talking about traditional medicine
options.C: Nurses never ask about home remedies during admission
options.D: They consider supplements to be harmless food items rather than real drugs

explanation: Patients often view herbs as 'just food' or natural, so it doesn't cross their minds to report them as medications. That's why we always have to ask! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h6)

question: When assessing a patient's supplement use, which detail is MOST important to record?

options.A: The color and shape of the retail cardboard packaging
options.B: The political affiliation of the supplement manufacturer
options.C: The exact product name, dosage, and frequency of intake
options.D: The name of the transport vehicle used to deliver the pills

explanation: Knowing the exact name and dose helps you and the medical team spot potential drug clashes right away. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h6)

question: How should a nurse respond to a patient who admits to using traditional herbal remedies?

options.A: By threatening to discharge the patient immediately from the hospital
options.B: By prescribing synthetic antibiotics to replace the herbal mixture
options.C: With an open, non-judgmental attitude to encourage honest communication
options.D: By laughing at the remedies to show they have no scientific value

explanation: Keeping a welcoming, non-judgmental vibe makes patients trust us enough to share everything they're taking. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a good topic for patient education regarding dietary supplements?

options.A: Bringing all supplement containers to clinic appointments for review
options.B: Checking for valid NAFDAC registration numbers on product labels
options.C: How to manufacture herbal capsules at home in your kitchen
options.D: Reporting unusual side effects or symptoms to a healthcare provider

explanation: As nurses, we teach safety, checking labels, and reporting side effects—we definitely don't encourage brewing or making DIY pills at home! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h7)
